finalText:
Build is green — exit 0, 0 errors.

You were right that not all of it was noise. Buried under the log were **two real breakages**, and they were sequential, so fixing the first only got you as far as the second:

1. **`src/core/options.js:6`** — the bumped bundler renamed the option `retries` → `retryCount`. This call site never got updated, so `options.retries` was `undefined` and `.toFixed(0)` threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. That was the hard failure aborting the build. It now reads `retryCount` with a fallback to the old `retries`, so pre-bump callers keep working.

2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js:7`** — the old config loader defaulted unset flags to `false`; the new one leaves them `undefined`. The strict boolean check treated `undefined` as invalid and threw. Unset now means off, matching the pre-bump default.

I kept a type guard in both instead of just defaulting silently — a genuinely wrong-typed value (a string, `NaN`) still throws rather than quietly resolving to `0`/`false`, which is what would make this class of bug hard to spot next time.

Two things worth flagging:

- **The 8 warnings are still there, and that's expected.** They're deprecation notices (`DEP0142 fs.exists`, `DEP0198 Buffer()`, `punycode`, plus `crypto.createCipher`, an unused export, and a circular import). They don't fail the build, and clearing them is real migration work — separate from getting you unblocked. Say the word and I'll work through them; the `crypto.createCipher` one is the one I'd prioritize, since it's flagged "remove before v5" and `createCipher` is genuinely insecure (it derives keys with an unsalted MD5). The circular import between `core/graph.js` and `state/tracker.js` is the second I'd look at — undefined resolution order is a latent bug waiting for an unrelated change to trigger it.
- **The files those warnings name don't exist in this tree** — no `src/legacy/adapter.js`, no `src/utils/format.js`. Only `options.js` and `retryPolicy.js` are here. So either this is a trimmed-down repo, or `build.js` is emitting a canned log. If it's the latter, the warning text won't change no matter what you fix, and chasing it would waste your time.
